questions.stem:
A CMDB Administrator would like to minimize stale CIs in the CMDB.
Which CMDB Health Dashboard scorecard displays this information?
questions.explanation: The Correctness scorecard on the CMDB Health Dashboard tracks stale CIs. Per ServiceNow docs, Correctness is a KPI aggregating Orphan, Staleness, and Duplicate metrics. The Staleness metric measures the percentage of stale CIs that have not been updated within a specified duration (default 60 days). Therefore, Correctness (A) is the scorecard that displays information about stale CIs.

In CSDM, key application service types include Application Service (logical), Business Application (business-facing), Technical Service (infrastructure-level), and Entry Point. Without the visible drag items, a precise mapping cannot be determined.

questions.stem:
A new custom class is needed to reflect a new application being managed in the CMDB.
Which roles are minimally needed to add this custom CI class?
questions.explanation: To add a custom CI class in the CMDB, you need sn_cmdb_admin (to manage CMDB classes) and personalize_dictionary (to create new fields/tables). cmdb_inst_admin (A) is not the correct role for class creation. itil_admin (B) lacks CMDB class management permissions. data_classification_admin (C) is for data classification. personalize_form only allows form layout changes, not the dictionary changes needed for new classes.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between an application and a server?
questions.explanation: In the CMDB, the relationship between an application and a server uses the "Runs on" relationship type. From the application perspective it "Runs on" the server, and from the server perspective the application "Runs" on it. The correct notation is Application>Runs on::Runs>Server (D). The docs confirm dependent relationships like "RunsOn" (e.g., tomcat RunsOn Hardware) are used by the IRE for CI identification.

questions.explanation: The CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard Playbooks (CSDB is the abbreviation used in the option) provide structured guidelines for troubleshooting CMDB health issues like missing serial numbers. Option A is not the official name. Option D uses CSDM (Common Service Data Model) instead of CMDB/CSDB. Option B refers to CSDM Now Create which is about framework content, not CI data quality troubleshooting.

questions.stem:
Configuration Management needs to ensure data quality for all CIs in the CMDB.
What areas of data quality for CIs are in the CMDB Health Dashboard? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The CMDB Health Dashboard evaluates data quality through three KPIs: Correctness, Completeness, and Compliance. Under Correctness, the metrics include Orphan, Staleness (Stale CIs), and Duplicate (Duplicate CIs). The answer choices B (State CIs, referring to Stale CIs) and C (Duplicate CIs) match the Staleness and Duplicate metrics under the Correctness KPI. Missing CIs (A), Downgraded CIs (D), and Upgraded CIs (E) are not CMDB Health Dashboard metrics.

The following Reconciliation Rules were configured for ServiceNow, Altiris, and SCCM:

Which are true? (Choose two.)

options.text: Data collected with a discovery source of SCCM can update any record in the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table because it has the highest priority number.
Data collected with a discovery source of ServiceNow can insert new records into the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table, but cannot update records created by Altiris or SCCM.
Data collected with a discovery source of Altiris can update records inserted by SCCM into the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table.
Data collected with a discovery source of SCCM can be inserted as new records in the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table.

questions.explanation: In ServiceNow reconciliation rules, a LOWER priority number means HIGHER precedence. (C) Altiris can update SCCM records because Altiris has higher priority than SCCM. (D) SCCM can insert new records regardless of priority - all sources can insert. (A) is wrong because SCCM has the lowest priority and cannot update records from higher-priority sources. (B) is wrong because ServiceNow has the highest priority and can update any record.
